text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibia press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Classes at the Mweshipandeka school in the north of the country have been suspended because pupils say they are "under attack by demons". Churches prepared to hold services to chase the demons away, but some residents believe only traditional witchdoctors have that power.
- Church leaders from eastern and southern Africa are supporting Namibia's Council of Churches in trying to facilitate reconciliation among Namibians.
- A workers' meeting at the Von Bach dam scheme have indefinitely postponed a strike.
- The Windhoek municipality said it will conduct a survey into why bus services in the capital Windhoek are not being used.
- The Namibian agriculture ministry said water prices would not be raised immediately with the partial privatisation of supply services, but the move is unavoidable in the long term.
